summary: Orléans is a deck/bag-building worker placement game where you draw followers from a cloth bag and place them on a personal board to trigger actions, gradually upgrading your bag with better specialists. It's a tight, satisfying engine builder with light theme and a strong sense of steady improvement each round.
praised: Clean rules for the depth it offers
criticised: Can feel a bit solitaire with limited direct interaction
Trading/event track bookkeeping can slow turns

interaction.kind: contesting shared travel/trade spaces and a common event/tech track
interaction.detail: Players move followers around one shared board and compete for the same limited town/trade-post spaces and tech-track bonuses, so being first to a location matters. Most of the engine (the bag of followers, its upgrades) is still built and optimized independently on a personal player mat.
interaction.said: Often praised as a tight solo-feeling puzzle ('efficient engine building') but reviewers also flag that trading posts and travel spaces on the shared board get crowded — 'you have to time your placements or someone else grabs the spot first.'

subsystems: trading-post network on the regional map
sources: VP gained on landing on marked development-track spaces
trading stations built and connected on the map
stored goods (wine, cloth, sheep) converted at game end
scoring.how_you_win: Recruit and place followers each round to advance along development tracks, build a trading-post network, and bank goods; whoever has the most VP once the fixed round track runs out wins.
